neighbours.label: The English word 'each' as the subject of a clause ('Each X ...' or 'Each of the X ...'): lights up on the verb or count right after it that says what every single member has or does. Quiet: the same clause with 'the X', 'every', 'both' or 'all', 'per' and 'apiece', an object 'each' (after a verb), and 'each' in other languages.
fire: Each student has a locker near the gym.
Each of the boxes weighs about ten kilograms.
At the festival, each booth sells a different kind of pastry.
Each player receives seven cards at the start of the game.
Each of the rooms contains two beds and a small desk.
In this village, each house has a red door.
Each team gets three timeouts per half.
The recipe is simple: each layer needs twenty minutes in the oven.
quiet: The students have lockers near the gym.
Both of the boxes weigh about ten kilograms.
At the festival, every booth sells a different kind of pastry.
All players receive seven cards at the start of the game.
The rooms contain two beds and a small desk apiece.
In this village, the houses have red doors.
Teams get three timeouts per half.
The recipe is simple: bake the layers for twenty minutes each.
neighbours.notes: Cold step-in reader of bonsai1/L24/N7206+ (labelled from its own tops and probes only). Test written blind by a label-only second author. Probes: 'Each X has/costs/consists of' ~0.2-0.37 vs 'The X ...' ~0.03; 'every' ~0.08; object 'each' and Spanish 'cada' quiet. Solver found no leak.

predictions: most fire sentences 0.15-0.35 peaking on the verb after 'each X'; mid-sentence 'each' weaker; near misses under 0.1
